### TAG-142: Example 12.3 Further abbreviated expression of a single return to place of invocation

**Status:** 🟡 Partial

## Software Notes

I'd table it. This is a different feature from [TAG-143](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-143/example-122-expressing-a-single-return-to-place-of-invocation), not just a testbench-wiring question, and connecting it now risks exactly the kind of scope creep that led to the `select`/`bag.zig` detour.

**Why it's different.** [TAG-143](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-143/example-122-expressing-a-single-return-to-place-of-invocation) had a named destination (`R<$X$Y()>`) — the runtime just needed to know how to evaluate the invocation and where to put the result, which is what the `select` action does. TAG-142's destination is anonymous (`<>`), and the invocation `$X$Y()` isn't assigned to anything — it *is* the definition's return value. That means:

* I don't know whether `network.zig`'s parser even represents this as a destination with an empty name, or as something else entirely. That's a parser-level question, not a runtime one.
* `Testbench.run` reads outputs by iterating `self.def.destinations` and looking each one up by name. An anonymous destination has no name to look up by, so even if the runtime could resolve the value, there's currently no path for the harness to read it back and put it in a `Presentation`.

So getting this to work would mean touching the parser's destination representation, `Testbench`'s output-capture logic, and the runtime's `select` handling all at once — three places, none of which we've verified together yet. That's a meaningfully bigger change than adding a vector file.

**What's not at risk.** [TAG-142](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-142/example-123-further-abbreviated-expression-of-a-single-return-to-place) already GHDL-passes today (shown as 🟡 unexpected pass, since it's tracked as `Partial`), so nothing regresses by leaving its Runtime column at `-`. The existing 4-stage pipeline, the `select` action, and TAG-143/TAG-177 stay exactly as they are — this would be new work, not a modification of what's already validated.

**Suggestion:** file it as a follow-up ticket (or a note under [TAG-142](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-142/example-123-further-abbreviated-expression-of-a-single-return-to-place)) describing the anonymous-destination / implicit-return-to-invocation-place gap, so it doesn't get lost, and move on. When you're ready to pick it up, the natural order would be: confirm how the parser represents `<>` as a destination, then decide whether `Testbench` needs a special "anonymous output" convention or whether the vector format needs a way to name it (`@vectors(X,Y : _)`, say).
